values.label: Nation-state
values.description: State-sponsored or state-directed actor, as attributed by sources.

values.label: Cybercriminal
values.description: Financially motivated criminal actor or group.

values.label: Single operator
values.description: An individual acting alone, per sources.

values.label: Lab test / evaluation
values.description: The "actor" is a research lab or evaluator in a controlled setting.

values.label: Researcher
values.description: Security researcher acting in a disclosure or proof-of-concept context.

values.label: Unknown
values.description: Attribution not established by sources. Unknown is a valid and common value — never attribute beyond what sources state.

values.label: Load-bearing
values.description: AI was central — the operation as described could not have happened at this scale or in this form without it.

values.label: Significant
values.description: AI materially enabled or accelerated the operation, but was one of several important components.

values.label: Incidental
values.description: AI played a minor or supporting role (e.g. a productivity aid); sources indicate it did not provide novel capability.

values.label: Disputed
values.description: Sources conflict on AI's role, or a vendor's framing of AI's centrality is contested.

values.label: Unknown
values.description: Sources do not support an assessment of how central AI was.

values.label: Tool-assisted
values.description: The AI was used as a productivity aid (code generation, drafting, research) while humans performed the operation. The AI did not act.

values.label: Human-in-the-loop
values.description: The AI executed steps of the operation but a human approved or directed each significant action.

values.label: Supervised-autonomous
values.description: The AI executed the majority of tactical actions on its own, with humans intervening only at occasional decision points or checkpoints.

values.label: Fully-autonomous
values.description: The AI executed the operation end-to-end with negligible human intervention. Rare; grade conservatively and only where sources support it.

values.label: Not applicable
values.description: The AI is the victim/target of the incident (e.g. agent-hijack or a vulnerability), not the operator — an autonomy level does not apply.

values.label: Unknown
values.description: Sources do not support an autonomy-level assessment.

values.label: AI-orchestrated campaign
values.description: A human-directed attack campaign in which an AI agent orchestrated or executed substantial portions of the operation across multiple phases.

values.label: Autonomous attack
values.description: An attack executed largely or wholly by an AI agent with minimal human intervention during the operation itself.

values.label: Lab escape / evaluation
values.description: A controlled test or evaluation in which an AI system exhibited offensive capability, escaped intended constraints, or was red-teamed into attack behavior. Not a real-world attack; pair with status: test-eval.

values.label: Agent hijack / prompt injection
values.description: A deployed AI agent subverted by an attacker — e.g. via prompt injection, poisoned context, or tool abuse — to act against its operator or users.

values.label: Infrastructure abuse / supply chain
values.description: Abuse of AI infrastructure, platforms, models, or the AI supply chain (model registries, agent tooling, MCP servers, plugins) to enable attacks.

values.label: Primary
values.description: Backed by primary sourcing — first-party disclosure, vendor incident report, government advisory, or court documents.

values.label: Secondary
values.description: Backed by secondhand reporting (news, analyst write-ups) without a primary source.

values.label: Unverified
values.description: A single unconfirmed source. Treat claims with caution.

values.label: Sponsor attribution
values.description: A cited source attributes the operation to a state sponsor; the point is that state's centroid. Sponsorship says nothing about where the operators sat. Origin points only.

values.label: Operator location
values.description: A cited source states where the operators were located or based. Origin points only.

values.label: Actor location
values.description: A cited source states an individual or criminal actor's country without claiming state sponsorship. Origin points only.

values.label: Infrastructure
values.description: A cited source states where attack infrastructure was hosted. Use sparingly; hosting says little about who or where the actor is. Origin points only.

values.label: Victim location
values.description: A cited source states the country or region of the target. Target points only.

values.label: Stated precise location
values.description: A cited source names a precise place (city, facility) for either role. Never a centroid: illustrative must be false, and a victim site is named only if a first-party or public disclosure already named it.

values.label: Jailbreak
values.description: The attacker defeated a hosted model's safety training/policy via crafted prompts, roleplay, task decomposition, or similar.

values.label: Open-weight model
values.description: An open-weight or self-hostable model (run locally or via an inference API) was used, sidestepping a provider's usage controls entirely.

values.label: Legitimate tool abuse
values.description: A sanctioned AI product or agent (e.g. a coding agent) was used for its intended capabilities but toward malicious ends.

values.label: Indirect prompt injection
values.description: A deployed AI agent was subverted through untrusted content it processed (email, documents, repository data, tool output).

values.label: None observed
values.description: No guardrail was bypassed — e.g. the model was used within policy, or the relevant control did not exist.

values.label: Unknown
values.description: Sources do not describe how safety controls were handled.

values.label: Reconnaissance
values.description: Target discovery and information gathering.

values.label: Resource development
values.description: Building or acquiring capability and infrastructure for the operation.

values.label: Initial access
values.description: First foothold in the target environment.

values.label: Execution
values.description: Running attacker-controlled logic in the target environment.

values.label: Credential access
values.description: Theft or harvesting of credentials.

values.label: Privilege escalation
values.description: Gaining higher levels of permission.

values.label: Persistence
values.description: Maintaining access across restarts or remediation attempts.

values.label: Exfiltration
values.description: Removal of data from the target environment.

values.label: Deception / social engineering
values.description: Manipulating humans — phishing, impersonation, fraud.

values.label: Impact
values.description: Destruction, disruption, extortion, or other end effects.

values.label: Claude (Anthropic)
values.description: Anthropic Claude models.

values.label: GPT (OpenAI)
values.description: OpenAI GPT-series chat/completions models.

values.label: Codex (OpenAI)
values.description: OpenAI Codex coding models/agents.

values.label: Gemini (Google)
values.description: Google Gemini models.

values.label: DeepSeek
values.description: DeepSeek models.

values.label: Qwen (Alibaba)
values.description: Alibaba Qwen open-weight models and derivatives (e.g. Qwen2.5-Coder).

values.label: Llama (Meta)
values.description: Meta Llama open-weight models and derivatives.

values.label: Mistral
values.description: Mistral AI models and derivatives.

values.label: Hermes (Nous Research)
values.description: Nous Research Hermes fine-tunes.

values.label: Other / unspecified
values.description: A model family not listed above, or sources do not name the model family.

values.label: Active
values.description: The current, maintained record. The default when record_status is omitted.

values.label: Disputed
values.description: The record's facts or framing are contested by credible sources. Kept visible with the dispute noted; grade cautiously.

values.label: Retracted
values.description: Withdrawn after the underlying claim did not hold up. Retained (not deleted) for citation stability; explain in revisions[].

values.label: Superseded
values.description: Replaced by another record (set superseded_by). Kept so existing citations still resolve.

values.label: Technology
values.description: Software, hardware, cloud, and IT service companies.

values.label: Financial services
values.description: Banks, insurers, payment providers, and financial institutions.

values.label: Government
values.description: Public-sector bodies and agencies.

values.label: Healthcare
values.description: Hospitals, providers, health systems, and medical data holders.

values.label: Emergency services
values.description: Police, fire, EMS, and emergency response organizations.

values.label: Chemical manufacturing
values.description: Chemical producers and industrial manufacturers.

values.label: Defense
values.description: Defense contractors and military-adjacent organizations.

values.label: Energy / utilities
values.description: Power, oil and gas, water, and utility providers.

values.label: Telecommunications
values.description: Telecom carriers and network operators.

values.label: Education
values.description: Schools, universities, and research/education institutions.

values.label: Retail / e-commerce
values.description: Consumer retail and online commerce.

values.label: Media
values.description: News, publishing, and media organizations.

values.label: Legal
values.description: Law firms and legal-services organizations.

values.label: Religious institutions
values.description: Churches, faith-based organizations, and religious bodies.

values.label: Critical infrastructure
values.description: Infrastructure not covered by a more specific sector above.

values.label: Critical
values.description: Broad real-world harm — e.g. many organizations compromised, large-scale exfiltration, or critical-infrastructure impact.

values.label: High
values.description: Significant confirmed harm to one or more organizations.

values.label: Medium
values.description: Limited or contained harm, or high-signal capability demonstration.

values.label: Low
values.description: Minimal direct harm; primarily notable as a precedent or signal.

values.label: First-party disclosure
values.description: Disclosure by the victim, the platform, or another directly involved party.

values.label: Vendor report
values.description: Incident or threat-intelligence report by a security or AI vendor.

values.label: Government advisory
values.description: Advisory, alert, or indictment from a government body.

values.label: Research paper
values.description: Peer-reviewed paper or formal technical report.

values.label: News
values.description: Journalistic reporting.

values.label: Blog
values.description: Informal write-up by a researcher or practitioner.

values.label: Other
values.description: Anything else — prefer a more specific type when possible.

values.label: Confirmed
values.description: Confirmed by a first-party disclosure or multiple independent credible sources.

values.label: Reported
values.description: Publicly reported but not independently confirmed. Never present a reported incident as confirmed.

values.label: Test / evaluation
values.description: Occurred in a controlled lab test, red-team exercise, or evaluation — not a real-world attack.
